answer: Agents streaming ocean observations from a ledge in a light zephyr earn relay quotas by measured bandwidth, not account count. Validators simultaneously send unpredictable, distinct data streams to each relay and require timely delivery to independent receivers. Quotas scale with delivered bytes, with no per-account bonus. Aliases sharing one uplink must divide its capacity rather than multiply their allowance. This requires honest receivers and resists cheap identities, not purchased bandwidth.
